name: My Jobs loads additional opportunity and application pages
description: Verifies customers and workers can load older jobs and application-associated jobs beyond the initial bootstrap pages.
steps: Sign in as a customer with more than 100 posted opportunities and open Opportunities
Load more of your jobs and confirm older owned opportunities appear without duplicates
Sign in as a worker with applications beyond the initial 500 application records
Load more of your jobs and confirm jobs referenced by later application pages appear
Attempt to request the endpoint without authentication and confirm access is denied
Use a page that contains application-linked jobs and verify each returned job retains the exact requested database ID even though keyed database reads return records without IDs
Exercise a result set requiring more than 500 keyed opportunity lookups and confirm requests are split into batches of no more than 500
Confirm applicant profile images backed by stored image paths resolve to usable signed URLs
expected: Each request reads no more than 100 opportunity records and 500 application records, returns updated cursors, only includes jobs associated with the signed-in user, and appends unique job cards. Keyed reads preserve the requested IDs by positional pairing, split requests at the 500-key SDK limit, and resolve applicant profile images from stored paths.

name: Discovery feeds load additional worker and opportunity pages
description: Verifies discovery starts with bounded pages and can append further results using continuation tokens.
steps: Sign in as a customer and open Discover
Confirm the initial worker feed is limited to one page and Load more results appears when a continuation token exists
Select Load more results and confirm the next worker page is appended
Search for a worker from the newly loaded page and confirm the search finds that worker
Sign in as a worker and repeat the flow for open opportunities
Load another page and confirm previously shown jobs are not duplicated
When one feed has no continuation token but the other still does, load another page and confirm the exhausted feed is not fetched again from its first page.
expected: Each discovery request reads at most 100 profiles and 100 opportunities, advances the relevant continuation token, appends unique records, and keeps search functional across all loaded results. A feed with a null cursor is treated as exhausted and is not restarted or reread.

name: Portfolio interactions find posts beyond the first feed page
description: Checks that a valid portfolio post can be liked or commented on even when it is not among the first 300 posts returned by the feed query.
steps: Create or locate a portfolio post whose record ID is known
Like the post using its post ID
Add a comment using the same post ID
Confirm the like and comment are accepted for the existing post
Try an unknown post ID and confirm both routes return not found
expected: Like and comment routes resolve the target post directly by record ID rather than searching a fixed first-300-record page.

name: Chat history uses bounded cursor pagination
description: Verifies message reads are bounded and authorized, while explicitly recording that global-table cursor pages do not yet guarantee chronological per-conversation history.
steps: Open a conversation as one of its authorized participants
Confirm the first response contains at most 100 messages and a continuation token when more records remain
Select Load older messages and confirm the next page is requested with the continuation token
Confirm the returned page is merged without duplicate message IDs; do not assume the page is chronologically older because the database cursor currently traverses the global messages table
Attempt to open another user's conversation and confirm access is denied
Load a chat page and confirm the client submits only the message IDs returned for that conversation when marking messages read
Load an older chat page and confirm its returned message IDs are also submitted for read receipts
Confirm the read endpoint rejects or ignores IDs belonging to another job and never marks the current user's own messages as read
expected: Each request reads no more than 100 global message records, returns the database continuation token when available, and only authorized participants can retrieve chat history. Read receipts use authenticated, job-scoped keyed lookups for at most 100 client-supplied message IDs and do not scan a global first-200 message page. Chronological ordering and completeness for an individual conversation remain unverified until the database supports a conversation-scoped ordered query.

name: SkillHub brand assets render on landing, onboarding and installed icon
description: Checks that the uploaded SkillHub logo and favicon are wired to the public app shell and install manifest.
steps: Open the signed-out landing page and confirm the SkillHub logo appears without a broken-image indicator
Open the sign-up/onboarding screen and confirm the same logo appears
Sign in and confirm the sidebar logo appears without cropping the full image
Inspect the browser tab icon and web app manifest icon path
expected: The logo loads from /resources/skillhub-logo.jpg in all three UI locations, while the browser and manifest icons resolve to /resources/favicon.jpg.

name: Sign in, complete profile, upload avatar and use the installed app
description: Verifies a new user can create a profile, upload an image, save a portfolio link and navigate the mobile app.
steps: Sign in as a new user and choose Worker
Complete the required profile fields and add a portfolio link
Upload a JPG profile photo and save the profile
Switch dark mode on and use the bottom navigation
expected: The profile photo and portfolio are visible after reload, the dark theme is applied and the mobile navigation remains usable.

name: Customer posts a job, chooses an applicant, chats and both sides can report
covers: live WebSocket chat and message receipts
description: Verifies the normal job flow from posting through selection and conversation, including reports from both sides.
steps: Actor A signs in as a customer and posts a job
Actor B signs in as an available worker and applies
Actor A reviews the applicant profile and selects Actor B
Exchange messages and confirm the recipient sees them live
Actor A and Actor B each submit a report for the job
expected: The selected worker is assigned, the chat is limited to the two participants, message receipt indicators update and both reports are accepted.

name: Worker creates a Team-Up and builds a multi-worker team
description: Verifies a worker can post a collaboration request, accept several applicants and coordinate a team.
steps: Actor A signs in as a worker and creates a Team-Up requiring two additional workers
Actors B and C sign in as workers and apply
Actor A adds both workers to the team
Actor A, B and C open the Team-Up conversation and exchange messages
expected: The Team-Up remains open until the requested number of workers is selected, then becomes in progress and all selected members can access the group chat.

name: Require mutual completion and one rating per participant pair
covers: one rating per job and recipient
keyed confirmation hydration in My Jobs
description: Verifies completion requires all participants and each participant can rate every other eligible participant once per completed job.
steps: Actor A and Actor B open an accepted job
Actor A confirms completion and refreshes Jobs
Confirm the backend stores one uniquely keyed completion confirmation per participant and does not append to a shared participant array
Submit both participants' confirmations concurrently and verify neither confirmation is lost
Refresh My Jobs and verify each participant sees their own confirmation state from the keyed confirmation record
Actor B confirms completion
Actor A rates Actor B, then rates Actor C in a Team-Up, and verifies a repeat rating for Actor B is rejected
expected: Each participant has one idempotent keyed confirmation record. The job stays in progress after only one participant confirms, becomes Completed once all required participants have confirmed (including concurrent confirmations), and My Jobs correctly shows the signed-in participant's confirmation state after refresh. A rater can submit one rating per eligible recipient, separate Team-Up members can each be rated, duplicate recipient ratings are rejected, and pre-existing legacy ratings still block a repeat for their original recipient.

name: Saved workers, job cancellation and permission guardrails
description: Verifies saved professionals persist and users cannot perform job actions outside their permissions.
steps: Sign in as a customer and save a worker profile
Open Saved workers and verify the worker appears
Remove the worker from Saved workers
Sign in as a worker and attempt to delete another customer’s job or report a job they did not participate in
expected: Saved workers can be added and removed, and unauthorized deletion or reporting is blocked with a clear message.

name: Team selection atomically assigns the worker and accepts the application
covers: concurrent additions do not lose worker IDs
description: Verifies the Team-Up opportunity and selected application cannot be left in conflicting states when a selection races with another update.
steps: Create an open Team-Up and submit an application from a worker
As the team owner, select that worker
Verify the opportunity's workerIds includes the selected worker and the selected application status is accepted
Simulate a concurrent change that makes the application no longer applied before the selection transaction commits
Verify the transaction does not add the worker to the team when the application update condition fails
Start with a Team-Up that has one member and room for two more workers
Race two applicant selections based on the same workerIds snapshot
Verify only one transaction commits, the other application remains applied, and no selected worker is lost
Refresh the Team-Up and retry the second selection against the new membership snapshot
Verify the final workerIds list contains each accepted worker exactly once and does not exceed teamSize
expected: The opportunity update and selected application status commit together. The opportunity patch compares both open status and the exact workerIds snapshot. Concurrent selections based on the same snapshot cannot overwrite each other: one commits, the other conflicts without accepting its application, and a refreshed retry can safely add the next worker without duplicates or exceeding teamSize.

name: Realtime subscriptions remain complete beyond global table page limits
description: Tracks release-blocking realtime scale and connection-ownership requirements. The current implementation is expected to fail the scale and ownership checks until the documented platform dependencies are resolved.
steps: Create more than 1,000 subscriptions across multiple job conversations
Subscribe a valid participant to a conversation whose subscription record is beyond the first global 1,000 records
Send a message and verify every active participant in that conversation receives the entity.update event
Repeat the same subscribe request and verify it does not create duplicate subscription records
Attempt to subscribe using a connection ID issued to a different authenticated user and verify server/platform ownership validation rejects it
Unsubscribe and disconnect one participant and verify only that participant's subscription records are removed
expected: Notification fan-out reaches all and only active subscribers for the target conversation without scanning the entire growing global table. Repeated subscriptions are idempotent, unsubscribe and disconnect cleanup are scoped to the authenticated connection owner, and connection IDs cannot be spoofed across users. Current code has a 1,000-row global read cap and no documented server-side connection ownership verification, so this scenario is a known release blocker and has not been executed.

name: Application creation is atomic with opportunity cancellation
description: Verifies the apply operation cannot create an application after cancellation has won the opportunity status race, and records the remaining global-page limitation in cancellation cleanup.
steps: Create an open opportunity and sign in as an available worker with a matching skill
Race the worker apply request against the owner's cancellation request
When cancellation commits first, verify the application transaction aborts and no application row is created
When application creation commits first, verify cancellation can proceed without allowing any later application to be created
Repeat the same worker's apply request and verify the stable application ID prevents a duplicate
Use a cancelled opportunity with more than 500 historical applications and verify the test detects any application statuses beyond the first global page that remain applied
expected: The application insert and open-status condition commit atomically. Cancellation winning first prevents the application row; application creation winning first remains a valid pre-cancellation application. Repeated applies do not create duplicate rows. The test separately reports that cancellation currently updates only applications found in its first 500-record global page, so later application statuses may remain stale.

name: Team-Up cannot bypass organiser selection through direct job acceptance
description: Verifies a worker cannot use the single-worker accept endpoint to bypass the Team-Up application and organiser-selection workflow.
steps: Create a Team-Up opportunity as a worker
As another available worker, call the direct /api/opportunities/:id/accept endpoint for that Team-Up
Confirm the endpoint rejects the request with a conflict response and does not change status, workerId or workerIds
Submit an application through the Team-Up apply endpoint
As the organiser, choose the applicant and confirm the normal Team-Up selection flow still works
expected: The direct accept route rejects Team-Up opportunities without modifying them. Team membership can only be changed through the Team-Up application and organiser-selection flow. This scenario is defined but has not been executed.

name: Team-Up organiser cannot apply to their own opportunity
description: Verifies the worker who created a Team-Up cannot consume a team slot by applying to their own post.
steps: Sign in as a worker and create a Team-Up opportunity
As the same worker, submit an application to that opportunity
Confirm the apply endpoint rejects the request with a forbidden response
Confirm no application record is created and the Team-Up remains open with unchanged membership
As a different available worker with a matching skill, apply and confirm the organiser can still select that worker
expected: The Team-Up creator cannot apply to their own opportunity. The endpoint returns 403 before creating an application, while applications from other eligible workers continue through the normal organiser-selection flow.
